newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.

text.p: QLD READY TO FOLLOW FEDERAL LEAD ON NATIVE TITLE
Queensland Premier, Rob Borbidge, says he was heartened by yesterday's native title meeting between the Prime Minister and state and territory leaders.
Mr Borbidge says he's now confident the native title uncertainty created by the High Court's Wik ruling will be cleared up in the coming session of the Federal Parliament.
And he says if changes on a Federal level mean changes to state laws are necessary, Queensland will act with urgency to give certainty to mining and pastoral leases.
He says no thought's been given to his state going it alone because Queensland has to work with the Commonwealth to get the solution it needs.
DYER STAYS TIGHT-LIPPED ON DEPARTMENT PURGE
In New South Wales, the Minister for Community Services, Ron Dyer, has declined to say if he favours a purge of his departmental heads.
The work of the department's senior executive has prompted adverse findings by a Government review which the Minister says will be a blueprint for reform.
Mr Dyer's office says two senior managers recently left the Department, but their departures are not being linked to the critical inquiry.
The Minister says the appointment of a new Director General is imminent, and he will work with the appointee to review the structure of the upper echelons of the department.
CONTROVERSY OVER TORRES STRAIT TREATY
The Australian Federal Police says it has had an officer working in the Torres Strait for six months, compiling a report on the area's law enforcement needs.
The investigation has come at a time when the region's Federal MP, Warren Entcsh, has been critical of the Torres Strait Treaty between Australia and Papua New Guinea.
The treaty allows indigenous people unrestricted travel between the two countries, but Mr Entcsh says it's being abused by drug smugglers.
Mr Entcsh says he'll be lobbying the Federal Customs Minister to review the agreement.
NSW JOCKEYS' DISPUTE PERHAPS NEARING AN END
New South Wales Industrial Relations Minister, Jeff Shaw, will meet this morning with jockey and race club representatives in an attempt to resolve the on-going jockeys' pay dispute.
Jockeys are seeking an increase in fees for losing rides from 65 dollars to 90 dollars.
Mr Shaw will meet with jockeys Shane Dye and Kevin Moses as well as members of the Australian Workers, Union and the Australian Jockeys' Club.
Mr Shaw says he'll consider appointing a mediator if the matter can't be resolved today, to the satisfaction of the jockeys and racing clubs.
TASMANIAN GOVERNMENT AFTER $200,000 FOR BRYANT HOUSE
The Tasmanian government hopes to get more than $200,000 for the sale of the home of Port Arthur gunman Martin Bryant.
Tenders for the sale of the house are being called this morning.
The Tasmanian Supreme Court has cleared the way for the sale of Bryant's assets, with the proceeds going towards compensation for the victims of the shooting.
Tenders for the house, in the Hobart suburb of New Town, close at the end of next month.
IN SPORT...
TENNIS
Players have presented Australian Open officals with a petition expressing concern at the move to close the roof on centre court at Melbourne Park.
Officals opted to close the roof following concerns that a player could be seriously injured because of the heat.
This morning the womens semi finals start with Amanda Coetzer taking on Mary Pierce, followed by the semi between Martina Hingis and Mary Jo Fernandez.
And in the men's first semi final Micheal Chang meets Carlos Moya.
Overnight, Pete Sampras made it through to the semis with a five set win over Albert Costa. Sampras will play Thomas Muster tomorrow.
And Mark Philippoussis could have a new coach by next week if Amanda Coetzer's coach Gavin Hopper decides to accept the job.
RUGBY LEAGUE
South Sydney president George Piggins and St George chairman Warren Lockwood have emerged as front runners to take over from Ken Arthurson.
Mr Arthurson yesterday stepped down from the post citing his health and the Super League war as the main reasons.
The ARL suffered another blow yesterday with executive assistant Greg Mitchell leaving to join the Australian Rugby Union.
Meantime the Canberra Raiders are in camp in Thredbo until Saturday.
RUGBY UNION
Brisbane Broncos winger Willie Carne will decide whether to switch to rugby union by the end of the week.
The Australian Rugby Union will call Damien Smith to the negotiating table next Tuesday in a bid to sort out his wrangle with the Queensland Rugby Union.
And the Brumbies will play a trial against Wellington at Kippax Oval on the 10th of February.
CRICKET
Essendon football coach Kevin Sheedy has flown to Adelaide to speak to the Australian Cricket side in the leadup to the fourth test against the West Indies which starts on Saturday.
Coach Geoff Marsh says the aim is to give the players a different perspective.
The Windies expect fast bowler Curtly Ambrose to be fit despite a hamstring strain.
Meantime, the day night shield game between New South Wales and South Australia starts today at the SCG.
GOLF
Big hitting American golfer John Daly says he's a definate starter in the Johnnie Walker Classic which starts gets underway this morning on Queensland's Hope Island.
Daly missed yesterdays celebrity shootout with a hip injury.
Bookies have installed Ernie Els as the favourite.
SOCCER
The Australian Soccer side has accounted for South Korea 2-1 in the Four Nations tournament in Brisbane overnight.
Mathew Bingley and Alistair Edwards scored the goals for the Socceroos.
Earlier Norway beat New Zealand 3 nil.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
